title: Going green – treatment outcome and safety profile of chronic central serous chorioretinopathy treated with subthreshold green laser

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 (article <license>, Dove Medical Press terms)

condition: Chronic (non-resolving, at least 3 months) central serous chorioretinopathy with active angiographic leakage and BCVA 6/36 or worse, no previous treatment for CSCR (including anti-VEGF or laser); 13 eyes of 12 male patients, Lumbini Eye Institute, Nepal, 2017-2018; prospective noncomparative consecutive interventional case series

groups.agent: 532 nm green laser in SP-Mode (subthreshold, 10% duty cycle), Lightmed LIGHTLas 532
groups.description: Single laser session over focal and diffuse leakage areas, sparing the fovea

series.baseline_label: Baseline (Table 1, row 7 'Mean' under 'Central macular thickness', column 2)
series.notes: Row labelled 'Mean', with 95% CI in the next row; visits at 1, 3 and 5 months after the laser session; per-visit n not reported; for the bilateral patient the second eye was treated after the first eye's 1-month visit and its baseline is at its own treatment

exclusions.reason: CI bounds are not extracted as values

exclusions.what: Table 1 visual acuity and macular volume rows
exclusions.reason: Visual acuity is not extracted; macular volume is out of scope

exclusions.what: Table 2 change in central macular thickness
exclusions.reason: Decrease reported as a positive number (not transformable) and the absolute series of Table 1 is used

exclusions.what: Table 2 gain in lines of vision and duration to resolution of subretinal fluid

notes: Measure: CMT quantified from a Cirrus HD-OCT 5000 5-line raster scan without a subfield definition: central_unspecified, device cirrus.
Role treated: the paper evaluates the 532 nm subthreshold (green) laser variant as the investigated intervention, contrasted with established yellow subthreshold lasers.
Statistical analysis text mentions a 3-month comparison while the endpoint is at 5 months; the tabulated values are means.
All eyes were treated once; no retreatment was given within the reported period (Results).
